To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an asymmetric, one-pot, three-component reaction for the synthesis of highly enantienriched masked alpha-amino acid derivatives.

the bispalladacyclic catalyst (1) activates the azlactone by a soft metal-metal bond, the Brønsted acids (2) activate the azlactones by a hard proton, and the Brønstead bases (3) activate the Michael acceptors by a hard proton.

we developed a novel, highly efficient and stereoselective tandem reaction of N-benzoyl amino acids with alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehydes, catalyzed by a bispalladacyclic complex, to produce highly enantioselectively masked alpha-amino acid derivatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new synthetic methodologies and the application of these methodologies to the total synthesis of complex organic molecules.
the development of new catalytic methods for the synthesis of enantioenrished organic molecules, in particular, those containing quaternary stereocenters.
the synthesis of biologically active molecules, especially natural products.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a soft bimolecular catalyst, a hard acid and a hard base cooperate in a tandem process to generate highly enantiomerically pure products.

the bispalladacycles are not just good catalysts for the Michael addition of N-acyl imines but also good promoters of the azlactone ring formation.
